prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app composition comp, 1440x1024
Primary request: Design the authenticated applicant dashboard for a Hackathons @ Berkeley multi-role portal as a living event operations binder named ‘Run of Show’.
Structure: a narrow saturated Berkeley-blue mast at far left with compact logo and icon navigation; persistent horizontal role tabs at the top reading HACKER, JUDGE, MENTOR, VOLUNTEER; the main workspace is one large cool-white active-work sheet taking about two thirds of the width and one narrow next-cues sheet on the right. The large sheet opens with ‘Good afternoon, Maya’, event line ‘AI Hackathon 2026’, a clearly dominant ‘Hacker application’ progress sequence at 72%, and a primary ‘Continue application’ control above the fold. The right rail contains ‘Next cues’, ‘Team matching opens May 18’, and ‘Application due May 30’. Show enough lower content to imply team matching and the operations feed continue below.
Visual world: premium art-directed event production runbook, not a SaaS card grid. Berkeley blue #3D68BB owns large regions, ink navy #0A2457, cool paper #F5F7FB, Ddoski gold #CA841D, brown #AB5E18, restrained coral #E68A6D. Role tabs resemble clipped credential tabs; status is expressed with small review stamps and ruled rows. Space Grotesk-like headings, Karla-like readable UI text, Space Mono-like operational labels. One small restrained golden-brown Ddoski stage-manager illustration tucked into the mast, not a hero.
Composition: decisive open-binder layout, dense but calm, precise alignment, real operational content, clear task hierarchy, accessible contrast, production-grade web UI.
Constraints: this must read as a usable dashboard screenshot, not a poster or physical binder photograph; no glassmorphism, no gradient mesh, no floating rounded-card collage, no fake analytics charts, no neon, no excessive pill shapes, no laptop frame, no watermark.
